boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Lehigh traditions centered on the annual Lehigh–Lafayette Rivalry and campus spirit.

cards.title: Race a decorated bed down Packer
cards.subtitle: Lehigh–Lafayette Rivalry Week
cards.notes: Form or join a five-person team, create a theme and follow the required safety process for this Packer Avenue race.
cards.short_summary: Costumed teams race specially designed beds during Rivalry Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh describes Bed Races as teams decorating beds and drag racing them down Packer Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires the event’s safety meeting and waiver, according to Lehigh Alumni.

cards.title: Take the 2.6-mile Turkey Trot
cards.subtitle: Lehigh–Lafayette Rivalry Week
cards.notes: Join runners, walkers and spectators for the campus route to The Hill and back to the Clayton UC lawn.
cards.short_summary: A 2.6-mile campus run that brings the Lehigh community together during Rivalry Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh identifies the Turkey Trot as a 2.6-mile run through campus to The Hill and back to the Clayton UC lawn.
cards.access_notes: Lehigh’s Student Affairs calls it an annual Rivalry Week tradition.

cards.title: Catch the Eco-Flame interruption
cards.subtitle: Friday of Rivalry Week
cards.notes: Keep an ear out on the Friday before the game, when the Marching 97 visits campus spaces to play Lehigh spirit tunes.
cards.short_summary: The Marching 97’s surprise classroom-and-campus performances mark the approach of The Rivalry.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh says Eco-Flame began after Professor Rich Aronson asked the Marching 97 to play during ECO 001 in the 1970s.
cards.access_notes: The official student blog describes the band entering classrooms before the game to play spirit tunes.

cards.title: Read the Rivalry bedsheet banners
cards.subtitle: Campus and nearby student housing during Rivalry Week
cards.notes: Look for the hand-painted displays during the lead-up to the game; admire the creativity while respecting residences and campus rules.
cards.short_summary: Large bedsheet displays turn windows and public-facing spaces into Rivalry Week messages.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh calls Bedsheet Banners a creative tradition displayed in front of residence halls, off-campus housing and offices.
cards.access_notes: View only from public or permitted areas; do not enter private residences.

cards.title: Meet the 50 Game Club at lunch
cards.subtitle: Friday before the Lehigh–Lafayette game
cards.notes: Follow Alumni Relations announcements for this pre-game gathering, where senior players and coaches meet longtime Rivalry attendees.
cards.short_summary: A Friday lunch connects the current football team with alumni who have attended at least 50 Rivalry games.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh says senior players and coaches have lunch with 50 Game Club members on the Friday before the game.
cards.access_notes: Check the current event listing for attendance details.

cards.title: Watch Fritz Lab crush a Lafayette beam
cards.subtitle: Fritz Engineering Laboratory
cards.notes: Watch for the ASCE student chapter’s announced event and observe the Fritz Lab testing machine crush a Lafayette steel beam.
cards.short_summary: A newer engineering-themed Rivalry tradition puts a Lafayette steel beam in Lehigh’s testing machine.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh identifies Beam Crushing as a newer ASCE student-chapter tradition using Fritz Lab’s 5 million-pound testing machine.
cards.access_notes: Attend only when the student chapter announces a public viewing opportunity.

cards.title: Join the annual Rivalry ritual
cards.subtitle: Lehigh vs. Lafayette football
cards.notes: Plan around the annual football meeting and use official Athletics information for venue, ticketing and game-day guidance.
cards.short_summary: The annual football meeting is the centerpiece of a tradition dating to the schools’ first game in 1884.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh states that the schools first played in 1884 and describes the series as college football’s most-played rivalry.
cards.access_notes: Game access and ticket requirements vary by year and venue.

cards.title: Wear Brown and White on Friday
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide school-spirit tradition
cards.notes: Put on Lehigh brown and white for a Friday on campus; no special location, registration or purchase is required to participate.
cards.short_summary: A simple weekly display of school colors links students, staff and faculty in campus spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Alumni describes everyone in the campus community wearing Brown and White every Friday as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: You can participate with clothing already owned; no admission or purchase is required.

cards.title: Open the Little Brown Box
cards.subtitle: Association of Student Alumni’s fall 5x10 event
cards.notes: Attend ASA’s fall 5x10 introduction to explore Lehigh history through the box’s tradition cards and interactive activities.
cards.short_summary: The Little Brown Box packages more than a century of Lehigh facts and traditions for first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Alumni says ASA hosts an annual fall 5x10 event introducing first-year students to Lehigh traditions through the Little Brown Box.
cards.access_notes: Availability is tied to ASA’s annual fall event.

cards.title: Mark Asa Packer’s legacy
cards.subtitle: Annual Lehigh tradition
cards.notes: Check the university’s annual events calendar for Founder’s Weekend programming and engage with the campus history it commemorates.
cards.short_summary: Founder’s Weekend is Lehigh’s longstanding annual observance of founder Asa Packer.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh says Founder’s Weekend has been an annual tradition since it was first celebrated on October 9, 1879, after Asa Packer’s death.
cards.access_notes: Program details and access vary with the annual schedule.
